messages:
logan (devex): Deploying the new JS quickstart to Edge throws a runtime parse error: 'Unexpected token export' from a transitive dep. Local pnpm workspace run works fine. anybody run into a similar monorepo -> edge surprise?
trent (eng-runtime): yup. usually means the bundle picked a file that's CJS or not transpiled to ESM. In monorepos, pnpm symlinks can hide missing published artifacts.
mika (pkg-team): which package is it coming from? could be our tiny util package that still only ships cjs.
logan (devex): stack points to node_modules/@ourorg/utils/dist/index.js line 1. that file starts with 'module.exports' but the error cites an 'export' token further down in a nested file. weird mix.
ivy (ts): probable cause: package.exports in that package might expose CJS for subpaths while the top-level import expects ESM. Bundlers for edge prefer the 'import' entry. If 'exports' only points to cjs, you'll get this mismatch.
trent (eng-runtime): also check that published tarball actually contains the ESM build. pnpm link in workspace can let you import the raw src during local dev but registry installs only see what's published.
mika (pkg-team): digging in... package.json has: "main": "dist/cjs/index.js", "module": "dist/esm/index.js", and an exports wildcard: "./*": "dist/cjs/*" — oh no. that wildcard could be forcing cjs for subpath imports.
logan (devex): that matches other issues we've seen. Any quick remediation steps?
trent (eng-runtime): short term: update exports to use conditionals for the root and explicit subpaths. e.g. "./": { "import": "./dist/esm/index.js", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js" } and avoid the wildcard mapping. Also add "./package.json": "./package.json" so tools can read it.
ivy (ts): TS caveat: ensure the "types" field points at the declaration file that will be published next to the ESM entry (dist/esm/index.d.ts). In workspaces editors may resolve to src/.d.ts but consumers need the published path.
mika (pkg-team): republished a patch that adjusts exports and includes dist/esm. pack-bot please verify the tarball.
pack-bot: npm pack produced package-tgz (sha: def456). tar contents checked: contains dist/esm/index.js, dist/esm/index.d.ts, dist/cjs/index.js. OK.
trent (eng-runtime): for the app build, also configure the bundler to prefer exports/module over main. In webpack/rollup set mainFields to ['exports','module','main'] so import conditionals are considered. For Vercel edge, confirm optimizer respects 'import' conditional.
logan (devex): did the redeploy go green after the republish?
mika (pkg-team): redeployed and tests pass on edge now. added a prepublish script to fail if dist/esm missing and a small CI job that runs 'npm pack' and inspects the tarball.
ivy (ts): small search tip for monorepo: grep for suspicious exports patterns: rg "\\\"\\.\\*\\\": \\\"dist/cjs\\\" --glob '!node_modules' || true
logan (devex): thanks all. i'll add a short blurb to the quickstart README about publishing sanity checks and the bundler mainFields tweak. closing the thread. :white_check_mark:
